description: The refusals a query declaration and a read of it meet (Phase 680, DECISIONS.md D263). Authored inputs, each `expected` computed by calling the pinned kit; no seed. `registry` holds the queries the vectors read, each a canonical declaration as a JSON string, in id order. `gates` is the gate table the registry runs: a gate answers the `decision` of its rule for a query, and `allow` for a query it has no rule for. Every refusal but the reader's is pinned as its query-error document, an object under `error`, as the seam codec writes it (the document seam-refusals.json certifies a reader of); no sentence is pinned. `declarationRefused` vectors read `declaration`, a declaration's text, with the declaration reader (lenient: an unknown member is read past) and expect `accept`, or `reject` with the decode `code` and the `path` to the fault: the members are read in the order $type, id, params, resultSchema, effect, timeoutMs, pageSize, where, orderBy, source, and the admission gate last, whose refusal is OutOfRange at the gate's path; the parser refuses every null and every number past the finite double range, InvalidJson at the root. `admissionFault` and `register` vectors state a declaration as DATA, because two of the gate's refusals no text can carry: `query` names a declaration of `registry`, and `id` (a string), `params` (a list of {name, type, required}), `where` (a list of {predicate, column}, with `cell` for a comparison and `text` for contains) and `orderBy` (a list of {column, direction}), when present, replace its own. A cell is {kind, text}, no text for a null, its text as it stands and never canonicalised (a float's is its shortest round-trip form, a non-finite float's the token in quotes, as the canonical float layout writes it). `admissionFault` vectors hold the declaration to the admission gate and expect `admitted`, or `refused` with `at`, the path to the member at fault, and `error`: a parameter declared twice at [params]; then each predicate in turn at [where, i] (an undeclared column, then contains off a string column, then a null literal, then a literal of another type, with no widening and a timestamp fitting a column at least as fine as its own unit, then a literal its column cannot carry, with the column layer's reason); then each order key at [orderBy, i] (an undeclared column, then a column named before). `register` vectors register the declaration into the registry and expect `registered`, or `refused` with `error`: an id the registry holds is refused before the gate. `validateParams` vectors hold `args` (a list of {name, cell}) to `query`'s parameters and expect `accept`, or `reject` with the first refusal: a name bound twice; then per argument in order an unknown name or a cell that does not widen to its parameter's type (an int fills a float or a decimal, a null fills any); then every required name left out; then every required name bound only to null. `dispatch` vectors dispatch a read through the registry, a `grant` (an identity, as query-grant-laws.json writes one) presented or not, and expect `performed` when the resolver ran, exactly once, or `refused` with `error`: an unregistered id whatever is presented, then validation, then the gate, a deny lifted by no grant and a needsApproval by a grant for exactly this read only. `referenceOnly` names the vectors no extracted model answers (a case whole, or the `vectors` it lists), with the reason; every other vector's `answeredBy` names the query model. `unreached` names each case of QueryError no vector raises, with what raises it and why.

error.reason: a null literal compares with nothing; test for absence with isNull
day: a date cell must carry a canonical ISO-8601 date, YYYY-MM-DD, naming a day that exists
at: a timestamp cell must carry a canonical ISO-8601 UTC timestamp, YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ or YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.FZ with one to nine fraction digits and no trailing zero, naming an instant that exists

amount: a decimal cell must carry canonical decimal text — an optional '-', integer digits with no leading zero, and a '.' with fraction digits only where the fraction is non-zero, with no trailing zero (build the cell with Cell.decimal)
the float NaN is not finite, and the wire has no non-finite float
